response.sql: WITH excluded AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-'), lab AS (SELECT l.ID, l.PT, CAST(l.ALP AS REAL) / l.GPT AS ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.ID NOT IN (SELECT ID FROM excluded)), per_patient AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM lab GROUP BY ID) SELECT COALESCE(p.SEX, '') AS sex, AVG(pp.avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(pp.avg_ratio) AS avg_alp_gpt_ratio FROM per_patient pp JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = pp.ID GROUP BY COALESCE(p.SEX, '')

assumptions.assumption: A patient is excluded entirely if any of their Laboratory records has U-PRO = '-', so only patients with no '-' urine protein result in any record are included.
The ALP ÷ GPT ratio is true division: ALP is cast to REAL to avoid SQLite integer truncation. Records with a NULL or zero GPT, or a NULL ALP, produce no ratio and are skipped.
Missing PT or ratio values are ignored by AVG within each patient, and patients with no non-null value for a metric are skipped in that metric's per-sex average.
A blank sex is a NULL or empty-string SEX value; both are grouped together as one group labeled ''.
Only Laboratory records whose ID matches a Patient row are counted, enforced by the inner join to Patient.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude only individual lab records whose U-PRO is '-' and keep the patient's other records, so a patient with one '-' record still contributes from the remaining records.
alternatives.sql: WITH lab AS (SELECT l.ID, l.PT, CAST(l.ALP AS REAL) / l.GPT AS ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE COALESCE(l.`U-PRO`, '') <> '-'), per_patient AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM lab GROUP BY ID) SELECT COALESCE(p.SEX, '') AS sex, AVG(pp.avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(pp.avg_ratio) AS avg_alp_gpt_ratio FROM per_patient pp JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = pp.ID GROUP BY COALESCE(p.SEX, '')
